# AngioDynamics Reiterates FY27 Outlook; Appoints Eric Honroth President And CEO - Update 

 By RTTNews Staff Writer ✉ (editorial@rttnews.com) | Published: 10/8/2026 7:36 AM ET | Follow Us | Join Us 

 While reporting financial results for the first quarter on Thursday, medical technology company AngioDynamics, Inc. (ANGO) reiterated its adjusted loss and net sales guidance for the full year 2027, based on its first quarter performance and current outlook for the remainder of the fiscal year.

For fiscal 2027, the company continues to project adjusted loss in a range of $0.29 to $0.24 per share on net sales between $336 million and $341 million.

The company said it expects a tariff impact broadly similar to fiscal 2026, excluding any tariff refunds, based on its current view of the tariff situation.

The Company also announced that Eric Honroth has been appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, effective November 2, 2026, succeeding Jim Clemmer, who announced his intention to retire after ten years leading the Company. Clemmer will remain with AngioDynamics as an executive advisor to support a smooth transition.

In Thursday's pre-market trading, ANGO is trading on the Nasdaq at $14.25, up $0.06 or 0.42 percent.

# AngioDynamics appoints Eric Honroth as president and chief executive officer

 9th October 2026 

AngioDynamics has announced the appointment of Eric Honroth as president and chief executive officer and a member of the board of directors, effective 2 November 2026. Honroth will succeed Jim Clemmer, who will depart the board on the same date but will remain in a consulting capacity.

The company have shared that the appointment follows a board-led search prioritising a leader with medical technology experience, a demonstrated track record of commercial execution and operational discipline to build on the company’s Med Tech momentum, advance its transformation, and drive sustainable revenue growth, margin expansion, and long-term shareholder value.

In a recent press release, the company shares that Honroth brings more than 20 years of medical device and life sciences leadership experience across markets directly aligned with AngioDynamics’ portfolio, including cardiovascular, endovascular, urology and oncology. Earlier in his career, he held senior leadership roles at Abbott Vascular, Becton Dickinson, CareFusion, and Boston Scientific. His leadership experience spans both North American and global markets, including responsibility for large-scale commercial organisations and global business operations, providing a proven foundation for advancing the Company’s strategic growth and value-creation priorities.

Most recently, he served as global president, Life Science at Getinge and previously led Getinge’s North American business.

“AngioDynamics enters this transition with real momentum, including a high-growth Med Tech segment, a strong balance sheet with no outstanding debt, and an operational transformation that is delivering,” said Howard Donnelly, AngioDynamics board chair. “Eric has done what this moment requires. He has built businesses, driven profitable growth, and managed global operations with responsibility for both revenue and cost structure. He also builds teams and leads with a genuine commitment to patients, and the board is confident he is the right leader to deliver long-term value during our next chapter.”

Donnelly continued, “On behalf of the board, I want to thank Jim for his exceptional leadership over the past decade. Under his guidance, AngioDynamics underwent a successful transformation that sharpened our focus and built a solid foundation for sustainable growth and profitability. Jim’s dedication to our team, patients, customers, and shareholders has left a lasting mark on the Company, and we are deeply grateful for his many contributions. We look forward to his continued contributions as a trusted senior advisor.”

“I am honoured to lead AngioDynamics at such an important moment for the company and grateful for the confidence the board and Jim have placed in me,” said Honroth. “The company has a differentiated technology portfolio, multiple growth drivers, and an exceptionally talented team. I look forward to working with employees and customers to build on this foundation and accelerate progress where we see the greatest opportunities to improve patient care and create shareholder value.”

“It has been the privilege of my career to lead AngioDynamics these past ten years,” said Clemmer. “Together, we sharpened the company’s focus, expanded operating capabilities, and positioned the business for its next phase of growth. I am confident Eric’s experience and leadership make him the right person to carry that work forward, and I look forward to supporting a smooth transition.”

# AngioDynamics Names Eric Honroth CEO as Med Tech Growth Carries Fiscal First Quarter

October 08, 2026 - by Victoria Lambe

AngioDynamics, Inc. (NASDAQ: ANGO), a medical technology company focused on vascular care and cancer treatment, announced on October 8, 2026 that Eric Honroth will become its President and Chief Executive Officer on November 2, 2026. The same morning, the company reported fiscal first-quarter results showing net sales of $80.9 million, up 6.9% from a year earlier, led by double-digit growth in its Med Tech segment.

#### A New Chief Executive for the Next Stage

Honroth will also join the Board of Directors when he takes over. He succeeds Jim Clemmer, who is retiring after ten years as CEO and will stay on in a consulting role to support the transition. According to the company, a Board-led search focused on finding a leader with medical technology experience and a record of commercial execution and operational discipline.

Honroth brings more than 20 years of medical device and life sciences leadership in cardiovascular, endovascular, urology and oncology markets. Most recently, he served as Global President, Life Science at Getinge, and before that he led Getinge’s $1.2 billion North American business. Earlier in his career, he held senior roles at Abbott Vascular, Becton Dickinson, CareFusion and Boston Scientific.

“AngioDynamics enters this transition with real momentum, including a high-growth Med Tech segment, a strong balance sheet with no outstanding debt, and an operational transformation that is delivering,” said Board Chair Howard Donnelly.

#### Med Tech Leads First-Quarter Growth

For the quarter ended August 31, 2026, Med Tech net sales rose 13.2% to $39.9 million. That segment includes the Auryon atherectomy platform, the AlphaVac and AngioVac thrombus management systems, and the NanoKnife irreversible electroporation (IRE) platform. Med Device net sales, by contrast, grew 1.4% to $41.0 million.

Within Med Tech, Auryon sales climbed 14.7% to $18.9 million, marking its 21st consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. Mechanical Thrombectomy sales increased 6.7% to $12.0 million, as AlphaVac grew 37.4% year over year. NanoKnife sales jumped 29.0% to $8.3 million, driven mainly by demand for prostate procedures.

Gross margin also improved, reaching 59.4%, up 410 basis points from the prior-year quarter. The company credited favorable pricing and the ongoing shift in revenue mix toward Med Tech. Tariff refunds received during the quarter also helped; without them, gross margin would have been 57.8%.

#### What Honroth Inherits

The results give a picture of the business Honroth will step into. AngioDynamics reported a GAAP net loss of $7.1 million, or $0.17 per share, narrower than the $10.9 million loss a year earlier. Meanwhile, adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $5.0 million from $2.2 million, marking the eighth straight quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA.

The company ended the quarter with $34.0 million in cash and no debt, after using $15.3 million of cash in operations during the period. It also reiterated full-year fiscal 2027 guidance for net sales of $336.0 million to $341.0 million, Med Tech growth of 12% to 15% and adjusted EBITDA of $13.0 million to $16.0 million.

In addition, Honroth will take over a NanoKnife program that is moving beyond oncology. The company received FDA approval of its Investigational Device Exemption for the RELIEF study, a feasibility trial of NanoKnife IRE in benign prostatic hyperplasia. The study is designed to enroll 40 subjects at up to five U.S. sites, and the company views it as a step toward expanding the long-term addressable market for its IRE technology.

#### Strategic Investment Summary

# AngioDynamics names Eric Honroth CEO as med-tech growth accelerates but shares tumble

 AngioDynamics, Inc. has appointed former Getinge executive Eric Honroth to succeed Jim Clemmer as Chief Executive Officer just as its med-tech segment delivers another quarter of double-digit growth, although investors responded to the broader October 8 update with a sharp sell-off. 

by Pallavi Madhiraju October 11, 2026

 AngioDynamics, Inc. has appointed former Getinge executive Eric Honroth as Chief Executive Officer, succeeding Jim Clemmer, as its med-tech segment delivers another quarter of double-digit growth, although the company’s broader October 8 update triggered a sharp investor sell-off despite the positive operating momentum. Representative image. 

AngioDynamics, Inc. (NASDAQ: ANGO) has appointed Eric Honroth as President and Chief Executive Officer effective November 2, replacing Jim Clemmer after a ten-year tenure that reshaped the medical technology company’s portfolio and operating model. Honroth will also join the board, while Clemmer will leave the board and remain available in a consulting capacity to support the transition.

The succession arrives at an important point in AngioDynamics’ transformation. First-quarter fiscal 2027 net sales increased 6.9% to $80.9 million, while Med Tech sales grew 13.2% to $39.9 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $5 million from $2.2 million a year earlier, extending the company’s run of positive adjusted EBITDA.

Yet the market response was severe. AngioDynamics shares fell 20.86% on October 8, closing at $11.23, before recovering 2.58% to $11.52 on October 9. The magnitude of the decline makes Honroth’s arrival more consequential because he will inherit not only improving operating metrics but also an investor base demanding greater confidence in the company’s future earnings trajectory.

## Why did AngioDynamics choose Eric Honroth as its next CEO?

The board said its search prioritised medical technology experience, commercial execution and operating discipline. Honroth brings more than two decades of experience across cardiovascular, endovascular, urology and oncology markets, making his background closely aligned with the products AngioDynamics is attempting to scale.

He most recently served as Global President, Life Science at Getinge and previously led Getinge’s approximately $1.2 billion North American business. Earlier roles included positions with Abbott Vascular, Becton Dickinson, CareFusion and Boston Scientific.

That background suggests the board is looking for a commercially oriented operator rather than a leader primarily tasked with another portfolio restructuring. AngioDynamics has already spent years sharpening its strategic focus under Clemmer. The next challenge is turning its portfolio of faster-growing medical technologies into sustainable revenue expansion and stronger profitability.

The company’s own language around the appointment emphasises that transition. The board has highlighted med-tech momentum, the absence of outstanding debt and an operational transformation that is already generating results.

Honroth is therefore inheriting a platform that is more focused than the one Clemmer began leading a decade ago, but the market is also demanding more from it.
